answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation company blog post dated 2026-07-01 (title: NVIDIA Unlocks AI Compute at Scale, Inviting Partners to Power the AI Infrastructure Buildout). It is a party statement from NVIDIA itself, with CEO and partner quotes from Sharon AI and Firmus relayed inside it. The source is dated 2026-07-01; no separate statement date for the partner campus figures is given.
answer.note: Material source claim: NVIDIA states it is introducing a new business model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers under a revenue-sharing and credit-support model, and that NVIDIA will earn both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity, which it describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. This supports a conditional view that NVIDIA's economics on partner-deployed capacity could include usage-linked revenue beyond hardware sales, and that NVIDIA may take on credit-support exposure to help partners finance capacity. This is a company-stated plan, not a reported result: the source gives no revenue-share percentage, credit-support size, contract count, timing, or financial impact. Its use is therefore directional, about business model direction rather than quantified revenue. Partner evidence: Sharon AI's CEO describes a collaboration with NVIDIA on sovereign large-scale compute, and NVIDIA says AI cloud companies are building DSX AI factories. Firmus describes building a DSX AI factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, which is expected to scale to 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs. That is a partner's expected build-out, not a confirmed NVIDIA order or delivery schedule. Baseten, Fireworks AI and Together AI are named as AI-native demand examples; the source does not say they buy under this model, so they inform demand conditions only. Counterexample check: every quoted fact could hold while no signed AI-cloud agreements exist yet, or while the credit support is minor, so the revenue-linkage conclusion stays a conditional hypothesis until contracts or filings confirm it.
limitations: No disclosed revenue-share terms, credit-support amounts or limits, or accounting treatment for NVIDIA's share of cloud revenue.
No disclosed signed agreements under the model; the source does not state whether Sharon AI or Firmus has signed or is procuring under this specific model rather than building independently.
The 360 MW and 170,000 GPU figures are an expected scale for a partner campus with no stated completion date, financing status, or NVIDIA-specific order volume.
The relationship between the named AI-native companies (Baseten, Fireworks AI, Together AI) and the model is not stated, so their role is demand context only.
Source is NVIDIA's own promotional blog post, so claims about scale and economics have not been independently verified.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's next 10-Q or 10-K filings for disclosure of revenue-share arrangements, cloud-linked revenue, customer financing, or credit support or guarantees tied to AI cloud partners.
Check Firmus and Sharon AI press releases or filings for contract terms, financing agreements, deployment timelines, and any NVIDIA credit support tied to the Batam campus.
Check whether NVIDIA issues any follow-up announcements naming signed partners under this model, with dates and disclosed commitment sizes.
